meta.title: LumiLivre — Management system for school libraries
hero.lead: LumiLivre is the complete school-library system: it catalogues by ISBN, handles loans, reservations and overdue items — and puts the whole collection in the readers' app.

problem.title: A school library does not fit in a spreadsheet.
problem.lead: Anyone who runs a collection knows: the hard part is not shelving books — it is remembering everything at once, every day.
problem.before.title: How it usually goes
problem.before.item1: Paper cards and a spreadsheet only one person understands.
problem.before.item2: Typing title, author and publisher for every single book.
problem.before.item3: Finding out about an overdue book when the student shows up — or doesn't.
problem.before.item4: Nobody knows how many copies the school owns, or who is reading.
problem.after.title: How it goes here
problem.after.item1: One single record, read by the library panel and by the student's app alike.
problem.after.item2: The ISBN fills the record in: you check it and save.
problem.after.item3: The return reminder goes out by email every day, without you.
problem.after.item4: Collection, loans and reading ranking in a one-click report.
ecosystem.title: Three pieces, one goal.
ecosystem.lead: The API keeps the data, the panel is where the staff works, and the app is where the reader discovers the collection.
ecosystem.pillar.aria: {{name}} — open the {{repo}} repository on GitHub (new tab)
ecosystem.pillar.api.title: API RESTful
ecosystem.pillar.api.desc: The service that holds it all: collection, copies, readers, loans and content. JWT authentication with three roles and an audit trail on every sensitive operation.
ecosystem.pillar.web.title: WebSite
ecosystem.pillar.web.desc: Where the librarian and the coordination work. Tables with advanced filtering, global search, light and dark themes, a guided tour on first sign-in and ready-made reports.
ecosystem.pillar.app.title: Application
ecosystem.pillar.app.desc: The collection in the student's pocket: catalogue with offline cache, the school board, reading ranking, guest mode and a session guarded by biometrics.
ecosystem.contract.title: One contract, three clients
ecosystem.contract.desc: The OpenAPI specification is published in Portuguese and in English, and the generated clients for the panel and the app come from it. An undocumented endpoint breaks the integration — CI checks for that.
features.title: What the library gets the next morning.
features.lead: Nothing here is a roadmap promise: every item below is in the system you can see in the screens further down.
features.item.catalog.title: Cataloguing by ISBN
features.item.catalog.desc: Type the ISBN and the record fills itself in — title, author, year and cover. The lookup tries Google Books, then BrasilAPI, then OpenLibrary, with a circuit breaker so one provider being down never takes cataloguing with it.
features.item.loans.title: Loans, renewals and overdue items
features.item.loans.desc: Due date, renewal and return on a single screen. Overdue items are flagged by a daily routine, not by your memory.
features.item.reservations.title: Reservations with a queue
features.item.reservations.desc: When the copy comes back, the next reader in line is notified — in the exact order they asked.
features.item.board.title: Content board
features.item.board.desc: Announcements, attachments and final papers with a target audience and a publication window: you schedule today and the board publishes on the date.
features.item.emails.title: Emails that send themselves
features.item.emails.desc: Return reminders and overdue notices go through a transactional queue: if the operation does not complete, the email never leaves.
features.item.reports.title: Reports and ranking
features.item.reports.desc: Six PDF reports, in Portuguese or English, plus panel export to XLSX generated inside the browser.
screens.title: The real screens, no touch-ups.
screens.subtitle: Captures of the running panel — in both themes, following the theme of this page.
screens.dashboard.title: Everything pending, on one screen
screens.dashboard.desc: Active loans, overdue items, requests and waiting reservations, with a monthly chart and the most borrowed books. The numbers come from materialized views, refreshed every 15 minutes.
screens.dashboard.alt: Management overview with loan indicators, monthly chart and most borrowed books.
screens.books.title: From the title to the copy on the shelf
screens.books.desc: Every title holds its copies, with an accession number and a physical location. List or grid view, advanced filtering by genre and status, and ISBN search.
screens.books.alt: Collection screen with the book list, covers and the advanced filter panel.
screens.loans.title: Who took it, when it comes back
screens.loans.desc: Checkout, due date, renewal and return in the same place, with the status of every loan highlighted and the overdue notice going out by email.
screens.loans.alt: Loans screen with the list of checkouts, due dates and the status of each loan.
screens.interest.title: What students want and can't borrow
screens.interest.desc: Readers can like a book in the app, and the totals become a purchase queue: how many want it, how many copies exist and how many are free. Without naming who liked it — the audience is under age.
screens.interest.alt: Reader interest screen with the most wanted titles, the number of interested readers, the copies on the shelf and the status of each title.
screens.ranking.title: Reading turned into friendly competition
screens.ranking.desc: Reader ranking by course, module and shift, with participation charts — the same ranking the student sees in the app.
screens.ranking.alt: Ranking screen with the readers' podium and participation charts by course and shift.
eng.title: The decisions you never see on screen.
eng.lead: The part that matters to whoever is going to read the code: what was chosen, and why.
eng.item.rls.label: database
eng.item.rls.title: Row Level Security on all 20 tables
eng.item.rls.desc: Every table is created with RLS enabled and forced, denying by default — even for the table owner. A query that escapes the service layer leaks nothing.
eng.item.ratelimit.label: authentication
eng.item.ratelimit.title: Attempt limits on two axes
eng.item.ratelimit.desc: Five attempts per IP in ten minutes, and five per account before a fifteen-minute lock. IP-only lets a distributed attack through; account-only lets you sweep accounts.
eng.item.audit.label: audit
eng.item.audit.title: Audit trail and access log
eng.item.audit.desc: Every sensitive operation records who did what, and from which IP — resolved from the proxy headers, not from the load balancer's address.
eng.item.outbox.label: email
eng.item.outbox.title: Transactional outbox
eng.item.outbox.desc: The email is written in the same transaction as the business change and dispatched later by a worker. A rollback leaves no orphan email, and a dead SMTP never fails the operation.
eng.item.resilience.label: integrations
eng.item.resilience.title: Circuit breakers on all six external providers
eng.item.resilience.desc: ISBN metadata, postal-code lookup and file storage all go through Resilience4j: a slow provider gets cut from the circuit instead of holding the request.
eng.item.views.label: performance
eng.item.views.title: Panel over materialized views
eng.item.views.desc: Three views pre-aggregate statistics, most borrowed books and loans per month, refreshed every fifteen minutes. The screen opens without scanning the loans table.
eng.item.metrics.label: observability
eng.item.metrics.title: Metrics in Prometheus format
eng.item.metrics.desc: The actuator exposes health, info and prometheus only — enough to instrument, without opening a management endpoint to the internet.
eng.item.csp.label: front-end
eng.item.csp.title: Strict CSP served by the image itself
eng.item.csp.desc: The container's nginx answers with script-src 'self', no unsafe-inline and no unsafe-eval, plus HSTS and framing denied. No inline script survives on this page.
eng.item.tests.label: tests
eng.item.tests.title: Testing where mistakes hurt
eng.item.tests.desc: Migrations and queries run against a real PostgreSQL 16 through Testcontainers, ArchUnit blocks cross-layer dependencies, and the panel has a unit suite plus Playwright with axe.
